title: ISS Water Recovery System
problem: Carrying fresh water for every use makes a crew dependent on resupply.
principle: The urine processor distils wastewater. A brine processor draws more water from the residue into humid air; the station collects condensate and the water processor treats it.
capabilities: The combined assemblies recover water from multiple waste streams on the space station.
limitations: The demonstration used the station air and water loops. It does not establish how a stand-alone Mars habitat would perform.
sourceTitle: NASA Achieves Water Recovery Milestone on International Space Station
locator: Discussion of the Urine Processor Assembly, Brine Processor Assembly and Water Processor Assembly

title: Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment
problem: A mission that brings all its oxygen from Earth must launch that mass with it.
principle: MOXIE took in Martian air and used electricity to separate oxygen from carbon dioxide. The instrument analysed the oxygen before venting it.
capabilities: The rover payload demonstrated oxygen production from the local atmosphere.
limitations: The instrument did not store its output or supply a crew.

title: Perseverance AutoNav
problem: A rover planner on Earth cannot steer around each rock in real time.
principle: AutoNav builds a terrain map from images taken as Perseverance drives and selects a path between waypoints.
capabilities: The rover can adjust its local path around hazards without waiting for a new command for each turn.
limitations: Ground planners still select the waypoints.
sourceTitle: NASA’s Perseverance Sets Off-World Record for Total Distance Driven
locator: Passage describing AutoNav and waypoints selected on Earth

title: Veggie Vegetable Production System
problem: Crews need a way to grow fresh produce where water does not drain through soil as it does on Earth.
principle: LEDs light the canopy while plant pillows hold growing medium and fertilizer and help distribute water and air around the roots.
capabilities: Veggie has supported plant growth in the space station cabin.
limitations: Cabin trials do not establish crop yields inside a Mars greenhouse.
locator: Veggie section, plant pillows and lighting

title: AstroRad Vest: CHARGE Evaluation
problem: A radiation garment designed for solar particle events must allow the wearer to work and move.
principle: AstroRad places shielding on the body. The CHARGE investigation studied how wearing it affected ordinary activities in the station cabin.
capabilities: Crew feedback can identify problems with fit and movement.
limitations: CHARGE evaluated human factors. Its results do not measure the dose a crew would receive on Mars.
sourceTitle: Comfort and Human factors AstroRad Radiation Garment Evaluation (CHARGE) on ISS
